generalfeedback.text: Pre-order (or post-order) supplies the root, while in-order splits left and right subtrees; that combination is enough for a unique reconstruction.

questiontext.text: In pre-order + in-order reconstruction, how do you identify the root of the (sub)tree?

answer.text: It is the first element of the pre-order sequence

feedback.text: Correct — pre-order visits the root first.

answer.text: It is the first element of the in-order sequence

feedback.text: The first in-order element is the leftmost node, not the root.

answer.text: It is the middle element of the in-order sequence

feedback.text: The root's position in in-order varies; it is not always the middle.

answer.text: It is the last element of the in-order sequence

feedback.text: That is the rightmost node, not necessarily the root.

generalfeedback.text: Pre-order lists the root first (and post-order lists it last); locating that root within in-order then splits the two subtrees.

questiontext.text: Once the root is known, what does locating it inside the in-order sequence let you do?

answer.text: Split the remaining nodes into the left and right subtrees

feedback.text: Correct — everything left of the root is the left subtree, everything right is the right subtree.

answer.text: Determine the height of the tree directly

feedback.text: Height falls out of recursion, not from a single split.
In-order of a BST is sorted, but the split is what reconstruction uses.
The split identifies subtrees, not leaf counts.

generalfeedback.text: In in-order traversal, all nodes before the root belong to the left subtree and all after it to the right subtree — the recursive split that drives reconstruction.

questiontext.text: Post-order combined with in-order uniquely determines a binary tree.

feedback.text: Correct — the last post-order element is the root, and in-order splits the subtrees.
Post-order + in-order is sufficient, just like pre-order + in-order.

questiontext.text: The pre-order sequence alone is enough to reconstruct a unique binary tree.

feedback.text: A single traversal is ambiguous; you need in-order too.
Correct — pre-order alone does not fix the tree shape.

questiontext.text: Which statements about reconstructing a binary tree from traversals are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: The first element of pre-order is the root of the whole tree

feedback.text: Yes — pre-order visits the root first.

answer.text: The last element of post-order is the root of the whole tree

feedback.text: Yes — post-order visits the root last.

answer.text: Pre-order + post-order uniquely determine any binary tree

feedback.text: No — that combination is ambiguous for general binary trees.

answer.text: In-order alone is enough to rebuild the tree

feedback.text: No — a single traversal cannot fix the shape.

generalfeedback.text: Pre-order gives the root first and post-order gives it last; in-order then splits subtrees. But pre-order + post-order, or any single traversal alone, is not enough.
